claim: Tessera improves throughput by 20%–33% over the production baseline across five workloads at 4,096–12,288 GPUs.
limitation: The headline production comparison is against Alibaba’s proprietary Megatron-LM fork, not a public baseline; the public Megatron-Core comparison is only at 256 GPUs, so the large-scale gain cannot be independently checked.
quotes: we compare against Alibaba’s internal Megatron-LM fork, the production training stack used for the same Qwen3-family workloads before enabling Tessera.
we benchmark against the Internal Optimized Baseline defined in §6.1
would_confirm: Release the internal baseline configuration or run the same five production workloads against public Megatron-Core at 4,096–12,288 GPUs.

claim: Tessera is a standalone library integrated with Megatron-LM and deployed in production.
limitation: No code or artifact is public; the 11,000-line Python/2,000-line C++ implementation and internal Megatron-LM integration cannot be inspected or run, blocking reproduction of all results.
quotes: Tessera is implemented as a standalone library (11,000 lines of Python and 2,000 lines of C++) integrated with Megatron-LM [22] (as a host framework).
We implemented Tessera atop Alibaba’s internal Megatron-LM
would_confirm: Publicly release the Tessera source, build scripts, and integration patches.

claim: Tessera is a holistic framework for trillion-parameter heterogeneous MoE training.
limitation: Production evidence covers only Qwen3/Qwen3-Next on Hopper/RoCE with proprietary data; non-Qwen models are tested only at 256 GPUs, so generality to other architectures, hardware, and datasets is unproven.
quotes: Our production evaluation focuses on pre-training the Qwen3 and Qwen3-Next model families.
comprising NVIDIA Hopper GPU servers (each equipped with 8 GPUs) interconnected via a high-performance RoCE network.
All experiments use a mixture of proprietary internal datasets and open-source datasets.
would_confirm: Run production-scale training on non-Qwen MoE models and non-Hopper interconnects with public data.

claim: Tessera’s profile-driven co-optimization systematically outperforms manual heuristics.
limitation: The only empirical comparisons are an internal Megatron fork and Megatron-Core MoE; no head-to-head results are given for Comet, DualPipe, Zero Bubble, Alpa, or other overlap/partitioning systems discussed in related work.
quotes: we compare Tessera against Megatron-Core MoE [36] on a 256-GPU cluster.
Tessera demonstrates that a unified, profile-driven co-optimization approach systematically outperforms manual heuristics
would_confirm: Benchmark Tessera against those systems on the same models and hardware.

claim: Tessera profiles post-overlap cost on a reference device group and reuses the plan across matching ranks.
limitation: Plan quality depends on the reference group matching the target’s GPU type, topology, and interconnect; profiling is offline and can take up to 3,050 s, and drift or heterogeneity would invalidate cached costs.
quotes: Tessera executes the synthesized schedule on a reference device group, a dedicated device set configured with the same TP/EP topology as the target rank, to measure ground-truth post-overlap cost.
Results are cached by device-mesh class and chunk specification for reuse across ranks and replicas with matching GPU type and interconnect pattern.
peaks at about 3,050 seconds at 128K for the trillion-scale PP8-C2 case
would_confirm: Compare plans profiled on the reference group against plans profiled on the actual target ranks under hardware/interconnect variation.

claim: The overlap-aware partitioner selects a partition that minimizes bottleneck post-overlap cost.
limitation: The MILP minimizes a maximum-edge surrogate, not the full pipeline critical path, and searches only a bounded neighborhood around the serial baseline; better partitions outside that space are not considered.
quotes: Tessera therefore uses the maximum selected post-overlap edge cost as a surrogate objective for partition selection.
Tessera restricts candidates to a bounded neighborhood around the baseline to keep overlap scheduling and profiling tractable.
would_confirm: Compare against exhaustive or full-critical-path optimization on small models and measure end-to-end iteration time.

claim: The Dynamic Bubble Optimizer fills routing-induced idle slots and recovers throughput.
limitation: DBO is isolated only on Qwen3-Next-M at 256 GPUs and 4K sequence length; production validation is two jobs, and controlled validation under infrastructure jitter is explicitly future work.
quotes: We evaluate DBO’s speedup, overhead, and memory cost on Qwen3-Next-M (256 GPUs, 4K sequence length).
Systematic validation of this extension under controlled jitter conditions remains future work.
would_confirm: Run controlled DBO on/off ablations at production scale and under injected network jitter.

claim: Static planning gave a ~13% boost and DBO raised Qwen3-XL MFU to 39.0% in the production trace.
limitation: The two step changes in a two-week production trace are attributed to Static Planner and DBO without a controlled A/B; other cluster, workload, or software changes could explain the jumps.
quotes: The first step-change (April 9) marks the deployment of Tessera’s Static Planner
The second jump (April 16) marks the activation of the Dynamic Bubble Optimizer
would_confirm: Randomize or repeatedly toggle Static Planner and DBO on the same production job and compare.

claim: DBO improves throughput with a bounded movable-task pool and acceptable memory cost.
limitation: Aggressive bubble filling caused OOMs on memory-constrained workloads; results depend on a per-GPU pool cap of 8 and available memory headroom, and memory-constrained regimes are not systematically evaluated.
quotes: aggressive bubble filling occasionally triggered out-of-memory (OOM) errors on memory-constrained workloads.
we cap the per-GPU movable-task pool at 8.
DBO increases peak memory by 2–4 percentage points of the per-GPU memory budget
would_confirm: Sweep memory headroom and pool caps, reporting throughput, OOM rate, and peak memory.

claim: Tessera’s event-driven overlap scheduler stays within ~1% of ILP on profiled post-overlap cost.
limitation: Scheduler evaluation uses only Qwen3-Next-M at 4K with EP8/EP32; the ILP reference often hits a 300-s budget without a proven optimum, so the comparison is against a truncated solver.
quotes: For Qwen3-Next-M at sequence length 4K, the EP32 and EP8 regimes produce 690 and 536 scheduling instances.
many hit the 300-s budget without a proven optimum.
staying within ∼1% of ILP on profiled post-overlap cost.
would_confirm: Evaluate on more models/sequence lengths and compare against exact or longer-budget ILP solutions.

claim: Co-optimizing partitioning and overlap scheduling yields the highest end-to-end throughput.
limitation: The co-optimization experiment uses a mock router with uniform token distribution and disables DBO, removing the routing stochasticity that motivates the design; production behavior may differ.
quotes: we employ a mock router that uniformly distributes tokens and disable DBO, isolating static plan efficiency from dynamic runtime variance.
would_confirm: Repeat the partition comparison with the real router and DBO enabled.

claim: Tessera introduces zero numerical divergence and no observed quality regression.
limitation: Bit-identical loss is shown only in one deterministic-mode run; no convergence curves, held-out quality metrics, or seeds are reported, and production runs are not deterministic.
quotes: The two runs produce bit-identical loss trajectories.
under deterministic mode.
the system has since sustained months of production pre-training without observed quality regression.
would_confirm: Release loss traces, seeds, and held-out evaluation results for Tessera and baseline runs.
